first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this because she wants to wear my mother's brooch. The intro says it will cover 'how to carry irreplaceable pieces safely across the world', and that's my question exactly, so I read on. Calm tone, short paragraphs, easy on the iPad.

journey.quote: Carry heirlooms, borrowed pieces and the sixpence in your hand luggage, photograph them before you fly, and check your travel insurance's per-item limits.
journey.reaction: Right there in the summary. Somebody has thought about what actually goes wrong. Good.

journey.section: 3. Something old: heirlooms with a story
journey.quote: Couples who plan well start the conversation with family early, because the best pieces are often in a drawer nobody has opened in years.
journey.reaction: That's my jewellery box. Nice to be part of it, not just the chequebook.

journey.section: Wearing an heirloom as it is
journey.quote: Have a jeweller check clasps and settings a few months before the wedding, so nothing gives way on the day.
journey.reaction: Practical and sensible. I'll do that this month.

journey.quote: Agree with the family before anything is reset. A grandmother may love the idea, or may want the ring to stay as she wore it.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Respectful of the older generation without making us sound old-fashioned.

journey.section: Wearing an heirloom as it is
journey.quote: Sarah Maria Wright married Daniel Neal on 27 July 1841 at St Nicholas' Church, Skirbeck, in Lincolnshire, in a block-printed cotton wedding dress that is now in the V&A in London.
journey.reaction: Charming, though more history than I need. I'd skim it on a second read.

journey.section: 5. Something borrowed ideas: who lends it and why it goes back
journey.quote: Agree with the owner how the piece will travel, who carries it and when it goes back, and return it in person after the wedding.
journey.reaction: Who carries it, and when it comes back. That's the conversation I'd want to have with my daughter before my veil goes to Italy.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Standard travel insurance policies typically don't cover items stolen from checked baggage on an airline, train or bus.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that. This is the section I'll print for my husband.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: A borrowed piece belongs to someone else, so ask the owner whether their own contents policy covers it overseas before it leaves home.
journey.reaction: That's me, the owner. Very fair point, and I'll ring our insurer.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around the day, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Payments is the word I noticed. But it doesn't say whether deposits to overseas suppliers are protected or quoted in Australian dollars.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing, before anything starts. That's what I need to see. I'd still want a phone call before we commit.

unanswered_questions: Are quotes in Australian dollars, and are deposits paid to overseas venues and suppliers protected?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day overseas, at 2am their time?
Can I speak with the Wedded Advisor by phone before anything is booked?
If the family pieces are with me at the destination, is there a safe place at the venue for them on the wedding morning?
would_share_with: My husband, with section 9 marked, especially the checked baggage and contents policy lines
My daughter, to agree which of my pieces go and who carries them

cta_reaction.quote: You will work with one Wedded Advisor, your single point of contact from the first conversation to the wedding day.
cta_reaction.why: One person and the fee in writing reassure me. This article is really about jewellery, though, so I'd click if my daughter asked me to, and I'd want to know a real person would ring before anything is paid.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, say plainly the first step is a phone conversation with the named advisor, before anything is booked.
In section 9, add one line on keeping heirlooms safe on the wedding morning itself (who holds them while the bride dresses), framed as a question to ask the venue.
Trim the 1841 dress detail slightly so practical readers reach the advice faster.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title and deferred business details not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: AUD quotes, deposit protection and on-the-day contact remain this persona's trust gaps, but business details are deferred. Treat as nice-to-have?

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and she owns some of the heirlooms in question.
Per orchestrator, brand voice does not discuss sourcing; the 1841 dress comment is about reading length, not sourcing.
